summary: bcore-bravo-eslint-config ships a load-time binary dropper disguised as an ESLint config
details: The package is published as an ESLint config (name bcore-bravo-eslint-config, description "environment config reader") but exports no ESLint rules or configuration. index.js unconditionally require()s./setup, which runs on load: it selects a platform-specific asset path (linux_x64, linux_arm64, darwin, win32 mapped to /pkg/package or /pkg/package.exe), downloads an opaque binary over HTTPS from hostnames reconstructed at runtime by joining split string fragments (`["oob-wor","ker.cf","99-9b3.wor","kers",".dev"].join("")` yielding an anonymous Cloudflare Workers host, with a `*.dl.well1.site` DNS-TXT fallback assembled the same way), writes the payload to a temp path under decoy names such as `dotnet_diag_*` / `.cache_*`, fs.chmodSyncs it to 0o755 on POSIX, spawns it detached via execFile, and unlinks the file ~5 seconds later to hide it. There is no version pin, no hash or signature check, the download hosts are unrelated to the declared publisher/purpose, and hostname obfuscation via split-and-join is used to evade static analysis. The name and description are a cover story for a generic binary-runner dropper that fires simply by requiring the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
